rationale: Small final source step on the recorded resume condition (membership/liveness) for the paused quorum candidate. The aliveness that gates broadcasts is connection-derived on each replica, not a heartbeat result: replicaListener marks r.Alive[rid] = false when the peer connection loop ends (replica/replica.go:465-472) and the connect paths set it true on a successful dial (replica/replica.go:157, 194, 409), while bcastCommit and the other broadcasters skip !r.Alive peers (epaxos/epaxos.go:578-606). The master separately pings replicas and exposes AlivenessReply.AliveList (master/master.go:118-132, 286-295), but the captured replica startup connects to peers exactly once in ConnectToPeers, and no rejoin, state-transfer or replay path was found in the captured files. So the missing-Commit precondition for the even-N recovery hazard would require a peer connection that is torn down and re-established after a Commit was broadcast, or a restart that rebuilds state - neither of which the captured code implements for a running replica. I record this as a narrowing of the A4 premise rather than a resolution: it makes the even-N hazard look unreachable without restart, which returns the question to the durability path (A6) where the confirmed CLM-DURABLE-BAL violation already sits, and it does not change the confirmed finding.

feedback.answered: On replicas, Alive is set from connection state (true on dial, false when the peer read loop ends) and gates every broadcast, while the master's separate ping result is exposed as AliveList. The captured startup connects to peers once and implements no rejoin, state transfer or replay, so a running replica cannot regain participation after missing a Commit; the even-N missing-Commit precondition would therefore require a restart, which places it on the durability path rather than on live membership churn.
